job.title: Territory Manager & Product Development Manager - Central Queensland
job.description:
The Company
Terranova Seeds is a specialist vegetable seeds company with more than 40 years’ experience. They supply commercial growers across Australia and New Zealand with a wide range of vegetable varieties and technical support. The business also exports selected products to the USA, SE Asia, PNG, the Pacific Islands, and customers in Europe, Africa, and Central America.
  
Partnering with leading international breeding companies, Terranova Seeds has grown consistently and become a market leader. With experienced technical staff, they provide high‑quality seed solutions trialled under local conditions to ensure reliability. The company is known for exceptional service, strong client relationships, and ongoing growth both locally and globally. Quality of product is their mantra.

The Opportunity  
Reporting to the National Sales Manager, this is a unique role that does not come along often. A hybrid function combining your sales and client management skills with product development responsibilities.
  
Your product development function will focus on the ongoing development of new products in the wider Queensland, gathering robust trial data forecasting and maintaining supplier relationships for existing and potential new commercial lines. You will do this by working closely with the National Product Development Manager, overseeing product development across the region as required while being highly connected to the end user, suppliers and client base in the supply of specific vegetable seed products. Focusing on crops such as tomatoes, peppers, cucurbits, green bean and sweetcorn. Overall, you are pivotal to delivering the desired products to an established and loyal client base while building a pipeline of products to introduce to growers in the future.  
  
Your sales focus is about business development. You will be to grow and develop revenue and gross profit within the region by sourcing and driving sales opportunities within the existing client base, while targeting new business clients for Terranova. Your selling skills and ability to influence and convert sales is vital for this role.   
  
You will:
  • Grow sales, volume and gross profit in the region to targets
  • Be present in the region looking for growth opportunities with existing and new clients
  • Spend the majority of your time client engaged developing sales and product development
  • Oversee ongoing trialling, development and launch of new vegetable varieties
  • Gather and report quality trial data to support new varieties (so you will be hands on)
  • Work closely with the product development team and sales team nationally to forecast sales, supply and inventory needs
About you

To be successful in this role you will ideally have:
  • Proven sales skills and experience in a similar environment
  • Technical experience in the vegetable seed industry and a sound knowledge of agronomy
  • Direct experience in running ongoing vegetable trial programs and reporting outcomes
  • Strong report writing skills with accuracy/attention to detail supported by exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • A natural ability and experience to listen and work positively with clients, suppliers, and growers
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications
Terranova offer a positive work culture where you will be provided with generous salary package including base, superannuation, car, phone, laptop and participate in the Company’s bonus plans. You will be expected to undertake local and international travel.

This is a unique opportunity with Terranova; an agile specialist vegetable seeds company which delivers tailored and ethical service delivery to its clients. A place where you have the flexibility to make decisions and lead by example yet work in a team environment.
   
For a confidential conversation please call David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply with a cover letter addressing the advertisement criteria and a fresh resume.

job.description:

As part of this, they will also develop relationships with dealerships, win direct-to-farm customers and authorised resellers.

Support, mentoring and leadership will all be provided to ensure that the products are well positioned for material growth in key markets. This is a unique career opportunity to introduce innovative products - that improve operational efficiency and add value for Australian farmers. 

About The Person:

To be successful in this position, candidates will require the following:
  • An existing network in the (NSW) agribusiness sector including dealerships and/or producers
  • Experience in agricultural sales / business development or corporate/operational farming
  • Excellent time management and communication/presentation skills (with the ability to run product demonstrations)
  • Commercial acumen and a strong sense of accountability
  • High levels of financial and career motivation 
  • The ability to work autonomously, whilst identifying opportunities for commercial growth
On Offer:

On offer, is the opportunity to connect innovative, value adding broadacre farm machinery and hardware, and precision agribusiness products with a captive and progressive market.

This opportunity will provide significant financial rewards and career development.
On offer is a generous salary plus a very attractive bonus scheme. This “work from home” opportunity also offers a large amount of autonomy and work-life balance. Equity (or similar) opportunities may be offered in the future.

To Apply:

For further information, please call Charles Linton on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au. All communication will be treated with the utmost of commercial confidence.

job.title: Quality Manager
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leading, large-scale horticultural business with integrated operations across farming, advanced packing facilities, cold storage, and domestic and export distribution. With a diverse multi-season operating footprint, the business is focused on operational excellence, sustainable produce supply, and continued growth.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the General Manager of Supply Chain, this newly created leadership position is based in Northern Victoria and plays a pivotal role in providing independent oversight of quality standards and quality assurance systems across the organisation’s national horticultural operations.

Covering multiple categories and production regions, the Quality Manager will own the quality framework from farm through to customer delivery, ensuring consistency in assessment standards, grading accuracy, food safety compliance, and quality data integrity. This role will operate across all stages of the value chain, including farming, harvest, cold storage, packing, dispatch, and third-party grower programs.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Owning and maintaining quality specifications, grading standards, assessment methodologies, and defect classification frameworks across commodities, varieties, customers, and markets.
  • Establishing and governing a consistent quality assurance system across multiple growing, storage and packing operations, ensuring reliable and defensible quality outcomes.
  • Defining and auditing quality controls throughout harvest, transport, cold storage, pre-sizing, packing, and dispatch operations.
  • Developing robust quality-loss attribution processes that accurately track grade movement and identify root causes throughout the supply chain.
  • Managing third-party grower assessment programs, dispute resolution processes, and quality compliance requirements.
  • Overseeing food safety, certification, market access compliance, customer claims investigations, corrective action programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Building quality assurance reporting and data governance frameworks that provide meaningful operational insights and support commercial and supply chain decision making.
About You
The successful candidate will be a technically strong and highly credible quality professional who combines scientific rigour, operational experience, and commercial awareness. You will be comfortable influencing stakeholders at all levels and capable of making independent decisions in situations where competing priorities exist.
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • A tertiary qualification in Food Science, Food Technology, Horticulture, Agricultural Science, or a related discipline.
  • A minimum of eight years' experience in quality assurance or quality management within fresh produce, horticulture, food manufacturing, or other quality-sensitive production environment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing quality systems across multiple sites, products or operational locations.
  • Strong expertise in specification management, grading standards, defect classification, food safety systems and quality auditing.
  • Experience working with external certification bodies, regulatory frameworks and customer quality requirements.
  • Proven capability designing and delivering competency-based quality training programs within operational environments.
  • Strong analytical and reporting skills, with the ability to interpret quality data, identify trends, and support evidence-based decision making.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to influence and drive compliance outcomes without direct reporting authority.
  • The flexibility and willingness to travel regularly across multiple growing and packing locations within Australia.
Why This Role
This is a unique opportunity to establish and lead a best-practice quality function within one of Australia's agriculture businesses.

For a confidential discussion, contact Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701. Applications can be submitted via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

This position reports directly, and works closely with, the Managing Director (MD) in all matters of support.  You will provide a wide variety of assistance to the MD, with primary responsibility to maximise the opportunity cost of their time by being ‘one step ahead’.  Trust with the MD is vital.

Responsibilities include managing priorities, commitments, correspondence, stakeholder relationships, briefing materials, travel and executive workflows to maximise leadership effectiveness and organisational impact.
  
Furthermore, duties include:
  • Act as the point of contact for the MD: calendar, phone and email management
  • Think ahead and anticipate solutions in advance
  • Schedule and coordinate MD and executive meetings and take minutes
  • Coordinate international and domestic travel arrangements for MD and general support to the CRDC team as required
  • Work closely with MD and at all times remain discreet and professional
About You
To be successful in this role you will need to be based in Narrabri and have:
  • 5+ years’ experience in an EA role
  • Have a reputation for being discreet, trustworthy, and able to work closely with an executive, yet remain a positive team player across the business
  • You are highly organised with excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Excellent attention to detail and used to ‘managing up’.
  • You have prior experience working well across all levels of internal management and staff, as well as external stakeholders
  • You are highly ethical, discreet, and understand the importance of confidentiality
  • As expected, you will have advanced level in Microsoft Office, excellent internet research skills, and be highly skilled at systems, processes, structure
  • Ability to prioritize, manage and meet multiple deadlines
  • Relevant qualifications will be highly regarded
This is a great position, working for a professional and supportive MD, who will value your contribution. A positive work culture with a genuine purpose. An attractive salary is on offer befitting the role and your experience.  CRDC has a team of over 30 and plays a key role in the cotton sector.
 
Please apply with your cover letter and fresh resume, or don’t hesitate to call David Jackson on 1300 380 701

job.title: Technical Product Development Manager - Home Pest
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an established consumer products business with a strong presence across Australia and a portfolio of well-recognised brands sold through major retail channels.

With an established R&D and innovation capability, the business is investing in their home pest portfolio as part of its continued growth.  

The Opportunity
Reporting to the R&D Director and working closely across Marketing, Innovation, Supply Chain and Procurement, you will lead the technical development and commercialisation of the home pest portfolio.

Working predominantly through third-party formulation, testing, regulatory and manufacturing partners, you will determine the best technical pathway from product brief through to commercial launch.

There is genuine autonomy. You will bring the specialist knowledge and commercial judgement to recommend the right path, challenge proposals where required and keep multiple product developments moving.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading technical development from brief through to commercial launch
  • Evaluating formulations, efficacy, claims, stability and packaging compatibility
  • Selecting and managing external technical and manufacturing partners
  • Managing APVMA registration pathways and regulatory requirements
  • Driving projects through stage-gate and NPD processes
  • Managing technical risk against cost, timing and commercial requirements
  • Building internal technical knowledge to support the portfolio longer term
The role is offered as an 18-24 month fixed-term contract. Sydney is preferred, with Melbourne, Queensland and other East Coast locations considered for the right person. Travel to suppliers, manufacturers, laboratories and trial sites will be required.
  
About You
You are an experienced technical or product development professional who understands how to move regulated products from concept through to commercial launch.

Ideally, you will have worked within FMCG or a fast-paced consumer products environment, with an understanding of stage-gate development, commercial deadlines and the balance between technical and commercial requirements.

Direct consumer or household pest experience would be highly regarded. Candidates from professional pest control, crop protection or related chemical sectors will also be considered where they bring strong product commercialisation experience.

To succeed, you will bring:
  • 5+ years' experience within pest control or a closely related sector
  • Experience developing and commercialising regulated products
  • FMCG, consumer products or comparable NPD experience
  • Knowledge of insecticides, rodenticides and pest-control technologies
  • Working knowledge of APVMA requirements and registration pathways
  • Experience managing external manufacturers and technical partners
  • Strong project management, commercial judgement and communication skills
A tertiary qualification in entomology, chemistry, formulation science, biological science or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

Why This Role?
This is a rare opportunity to become the technical specialist behind a new product category within an established consumer business. You’ll have the scope to influence the technical direction, manage the right external partners and see a portfolio move from concept through to products in market.

For someone who knows the pest-control market and enjoys the pace of product commercialisation, there is plenty here to get hold of.

For more information or a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha-Lima on 1300 380 701 or apply via Rimfire Resources.

job.title: Manufacturing Supervisor
job.description:

The Manufacturing Supervisor will support the day-to-day running of the workshop, helping the team complete work safely, efficiently and to the required standard.

This hands-on role suits someone ready to take the next step into supervision. You will help organise priorities, guide the team and resolve routine production issues while remaining involved on the workshop floor.

  • Help plan daily workshop activities and priorities
  • Allocate tasks and follow jobs through to completion
  • Provide practical support and direction to workshop employees
  • Monitor quality, output and delivery timeframes
  • Ensure drawings and job requirements are followed

  • Assist with equipment and production issues
  • Keep simple production records and communicate progress

This role will suit a reliable manufacturing or fabrication professional with some experience guiding others and an interest in developing their supervisory skills.

job.title: Discharge Supervisor
job.description:
The Company
Fertiglobe is a global leader in nitrogen-based solutions, supplying essential fertilisers that support agriculture and a more sustainable future. In Australia, its integrated manufacturing, blending, storage and distribution network serves major agricultural sectors across the east and southern coasts.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Shipping Manager, the Discharge Supervisor will plan, coordinate and oversee bulk fertiliser vessel discharges across eastern Australia. Based primarily in Port Melbourne, the role combines office-based planning and stakeholder coordination with targeted port attendance to deliver safe, efficient and cost-effective vessel turnarounds.

You will manage discharge plans, schedules, contractors and changing operational conditions. Active discharges require time-sensitive support outside standard hours, including some early mornings, evenings and weekends.
Additional key responsibilities include:
  • Develop discharge plans and monitor vessel movements, port activity and warehouse readiness.
  • Coordinate shipping agents, stevedores, transport providers, warehouse operators and internal teams.
  • Analyse performance, address delays and improve contractor, time and cost outcomes.
  • Maintain oversight of safety, product integrity, environmental obligations and regulatory compliance.
  • Complete operational reporting and attend ports as required.
The Person
We are seeking a commercially minded logistics professional with sound judgement, strong stakeholder skills and a clear focus on safety, service and efficiency.
  • Experience in vessel discharge, port logistics, stevedoring, transport coordination, shipping agency or a related environment.
  • Strong planning, analytical and problem-solving capability.
  • Knowledge of OHS, Chain of Responsibility, maritime safety and environmental compliance.
  • Commercial awareness, attention to detail and confident stakeholder communication.
  • A current driver’s licence and willingness to travel to ports and operational sites.
Why this role?
This newly established role offers genuine ownership of discharge outcomes and the opportunity to improve contractor performance and operational decision-making across Fertiglobe’s Australian supply chain network. Practical onboarding will be provided, with responsibility growing in line with capability.

For further information or an initial confidential discussion, please call Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Accountant - Agribusiness
job.description:
The Company

CHS Broadbent is a leading Australian agribusiness supply chain company with grain marketing, storage, logistics and export operations on the east coast of Australia. CHS Broadbent own and operate grain storage, container packing, and grain freight operations through Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria. They are widely recognised by grain producers and markets as leaders in providing reliable, dependable, customer focused service.

The Opportunity

As part of their continued growth, CHS Broadbent are looking for a Accountant to join their Finance team. This role will support the financial control, accounting, reporting and analysis of CHS Broadbent’s grain trading activities, providing independent oversight across commodity positions, grain inventories, mark-to-market valuations, profit and loss reporting, hedging activities and trading exposures.

Working closely with the Trading, Risk, Logistics, Operations and Finance teams, you will support commercial decision-making while ensuring compliance with accounting standards, internal controls and risk management frameworks. The role will be involved in weekly and monthly grain and trading P&L reporting, inventory reconciliations, commodity valuations, management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and process improvement initiatives including integration of AI tools and identifying new opportunities and solutions previously not explored.

About You

To be successful in this position you will have:
  • A degree in Accounting, Finance or Commerce, with CPA or CA qualification.
  • Experience in commercial accounting, management accounting, commodity accounting or a related finance role.
  • Strong understanding of inventory reconciliation, financial reporting, P&L analysis and management accounting.
  • Exposure to grain, commodity trading, logistics or agribusiness operations would be highly regarded.
  • Strong analytical capability, attention to detail and confidence working with large volumes of financial and operational data.
  • Advanced Excel skills, with experience using ERP systems, commodity trading platforms, Power Query, Power BI or similar reporting tools beneficial.

The role will ensure new wheat varieties, agronomic practices and research outcomes are effectively evaluated, communicated and adopted across farming systems. Just as importantly, it will bring market, technical and grower feedback back into the breeding program to help shape pipeline and portfolio decisions.

Key areas of focus include:

  • Delivering field days, workshops, technical updates and industry presentations
  • Building relationships with growers, agronomists, consultants, seed companies and industry bodies
  • Supporting product advancement, variety release and commercialisation planning
  • Providing technical, market and farming system feedback to breeders and the commercial team
This position will also play an important role in LongReach’s engagement with the NVT program, grower groups, retail agronomy networks, independent agronomists and key industry events across South Australia and Victoria.

About You

We are seeking a practical, technically strong and relationship-driven grains professional who brings:
  • 5+ years’ experience in cereal agronomy, broadacre cropping or a related technical environment
  • A graduate qualification in agriculture, agronomy or a related discipline
  • Strong knowledge of Southern Region farming systems across South Australia and Victoria
  • Experience in field agronomics, cereal farming methods, disease assessment and trial evaluation
